curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42113-1/ (scans of the four books' pages; the functions are shown on pages 333-335: the finished model in both modes, the four motor functions and the four red selector buttons with their stickers)

functions.does: The motor in the fuselage, run from the hub, drives whichever function is selected by four red push buttons on the fuselage sides (two each side, behind the wing): each button slides a driving ring in a gearbox under the wing, connecting that function's shaft to the motor.
functions.source: book: pages 333-335 (the four functions with the motor icon, and the four buttons with their stickers: rotors, landing gear, nacelle tilt, ramp), steps 10-22 (the hub and motor in the fuselage), the wing base gearbox (pages around 150-200)
functions.note: the buttons are p591, p594, p944 and p955 (42113 - 51149); which button is which function is read from the stickers on page 335 (upper left pair: rotors and landing gear; lower pair: nacelle tilt and ramp) and is unsure. Each function below is worked by the motor with its button pushed in

functions.does: With the rotor button pushed in, the motor spins both three-bladed rotors together, in opposite directions, through shafts out along the wing and up into the nacelles.
functions.source: book: page 335 (the rotor sticker), page 333 (both modes), steps 396-417 (the rotors on their hubs, pages 316-332)
functions.note: that the rotors turn opposite ways is inferred from the real aircraft; the owner should check. Unsure whether the rotor sticker means spinning or the blades folding

functions.does: With the nacelle button pushed in, the motor tilts both engine nacelles together between upright (helicopter mode) and level (aeroplane mode), turning them on turntables at the wingtips.
functions.source: book: pages 333-334 (the two modes, and the tilt with the motor icon), page 335 (the orange nacelle sticker), the turntables p1346 and p1480 at the wing tips

functions.does: With the landing gear button pushed in, the motor retracts and lowers the three landing gear legs: a linear actuator in the fuselage pushes a linkage that folds the two main legs and the nose leg up into the fuselage.
functions.source: book: page 334 (middle: the main gear folding, with arrows), page 335 (the landing gear sticker), steps 12-22 (the gear legs), the actuator in the motor submodel
functions.note: which actuator works the gear and which the ramp is inferred from where they sit: p882 alongside the motor, p974 at the tail

functions.does: With the ramp button pushed in, the motor opens and closes the rear cargo ramp: a linear actuator at the tail lowers the ramp and lifts the upper tail door.
functions.source: book: page 334 (bottom: the ramp closed and open, with the motor icon), page 335 (the ramp sticker), the hatch submodels

functions.does: The wheels on the three landing gear legs roll freely.
The rotor blades are hinged at their roots and can be folded by hand.
functions.source: inferred: each blade (42113 - 65422) is held on its hub by a pin with a stop bush (steps 396-412) rather than an axle
functions.note: unsure whether the blades are meant to fold; the owner should check

functions.does: The flaps on the wings' trailing edges move with the nacelles.
functions.source: inferred: the flap submodels (flap1, flap2) are linked to the nacelle tilt mechanism at the wing tips
functions.note: unsure: whether the flaps are linked to the nacelles or simply hinged; the owner should check
